title: Perfect Roast Chicken
description: A whole chicken roasted over fennel and onions with lemon and thyme.
steps: Heat the oven to 425F. Pat the chicken thoroughly dry inside and out and season the cavity generously with salt and pepper.
Stuff the cavity with the thyme, both lemon halves and the halved garlic head, then tie the legs together with twine and tuck the wing tips under.
Brush the whole bird with melted butter and season the outside heavily. Salt on dry skin is what gives you the crisp, burnished finish.
Toss the onion and fennel with the olive oil, salt and pepper and spread them in a roasting pan. Set the chicken on top so the vegetables catch the fat.
Roast 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours, until the juices run clear when you cut between the leg and thigh and the thigh reads 175F.
Cover loosely with foil and rest 20 minutes before carving. Serve with the roasted vegetables and the pan juices.

title: Lemon Chicken Breasts
description: Chicken breasts baked over a white wine, lemon and thyme sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 400F. Warm the olive oil in a small pan and cook the garlic 1 minute, just until fragrant - do not brown it.
Take it off the heat and add the wine, lemon zest, lemon juice, oregano, thyme and 1 tsp salt. Pour this into a baking dish.
Pat the chicken dry and arrange it skin-side up in the dish, sitting above the liquid so the skin stays clear and crisps.
Brush the skin with olive oil and season generously with the remaining salt and the pepper.
Tuck the lemon slices around the chicken and dot with butter.
Bake 35-40 minutes to 160F internal, then rest 5 minutes and serve with plenty of the pan sauce spooned over.

title: Beef Bourguignon
description: Beef braised in Burgundy with bacon, pearl onions and mushrooms.
ingredients: 3 lb beef chuck, cut in 1 1/2-inch cubes
steps: Render the bacon in the olive oil in a Dutch oven, then lift it out. Pat the beef completely dry, season, and brown it in the bacon fat in single-layer batches - crowding the pot steams the meat and you lose the crust that flavors everything.
Add the carrots and onions and cook 10 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Pour in the cognac, stand back, and let it cook off for a minute. Add the wine, broth, tomato paste, thyme and the bacon, scraping the bottom clean.
Bring to a simmer, cover and braise at 325F for about 1 1/4 hours, until the beef is fork-tender.
Mash the flour and butter into a paste and stir it into the pot. This beurre manie thickens the sauce at the end without any lumps.
Sauté the pearl onions and mushrooms in butter until browned, add them to the pot and simmer uncovered 15 minutes. Finish with parsley and serve over noodles or with crusty bread.

title: Outrageous Brownies
description: Dense fudgy brownies with a pound of chocolate and toasted walnuts.
ingredients: 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips, for folding in
steps: Heat the oven to 350F and butter and flour a 12x18 sheet pan. Toast the walnuts 8 minutes and set aside.
Melt the butter, the pound of chocolate chips and the unsweetened chocolate together over low heat, then cool for 10 minutes. Hot chocolate will scramble the eggs.
Whisk the eggs, instant coffee, vanilla and sugar together, then stir in the cooled chocolate. The coffee is not there to taste of coffee - it makes the chocolate taste deeper.
Sift 1 cup of the flour with the baking powder and salt and stir it in just until combined.
Toss the walnuts and remaining chocolate chips with the last 1/4 cup flour - coating them keeps them suspended instead of sinking - then fold them through.
Spread in the pan and bake 30 minutes. A toothpick should come out with moist crumbs; if it looks wet, give it 5 more minutes. Cool completely before cutting.

title: Coq au Vin
description: Chicken braised in red wine with bacon, brandy and pearl onions.
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (4 lb), cut in 8 pieces
1 lb carrots, cut in thick diagonal slices
steps: Render the bacon in the olive oil in a Dutch oven and lift it out. Pat the chicken dry, season well and brown it in the fat, skin-side down first, 5 minutes per side. Work in batches.
Add the carrots, onion, garlic, salt and pepper to the pot and cook 10 minutes.
Return the chicken and bacon, add the cognac and let it cook off, then the wine, broth and thyme. The liquid should almost cover the chicken.
Bring to a simmer, cover and braise at 250F for 30-40 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and tender.
Mash the butter and flour together and stir the paste into the simmering liquid to thicken it.
Brown the pearl onions and mushrooms in butter in a separate pan, add them to the pot and simmer 10 minutes uncovered. Finish with parsley.

title: Roasted Winter Vegetables
description: Root vegetables roasted hot until caramelized, tossed with herbs.
steps: Heat the oven to 425F. Cut everything to roughly the same size so it all finishes together.
Toss the vegetables with the olive oil, salt and pepper in a large bowl, using your hands so every piece is coated.
Divide between two sheet pans in a single layer. Two pans rather than one crowded pan is the difference between roasting and steaming.
Roast 40-45 minutes, turning once halfway through, until browned at the edges and tender.
Toss the hot vegetables with the thyme and balsamic vinegar.
Taste for salt and finish with parsley. Serve hot or at room temperature.

title: Grown-Up Mac and Cheese
description: Gruyere and cheddar sauce with tomato slices and a crisp bread topping.
steps: Heat the oven to 375F. Boil the pasta 2 minutes short of the package time, since it finishes in the oven, then drain.
Warm the milk in a saucepan - adding cold milk to a roux makes lumps.
Melt 8 tbsp butter in a large pot, whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes until it smells nutty but stays pale. Whisk in the hot milk in a steady stream and cook 2-3 minutes until thick.
Take the pot off the heat before adding both cheeses, the nutmeg, salt and pepper. Direct heat makes cheese sauce grainy.
Fold in the pasta and pour into a baking dish. Lay the tomato slices over the top.
Toss the breadcrumbs with the melted butter, scatter over, and bake 30-35 minutes until bubbling and browned.

title: Lemon Bars
description: Shortbread crust under a thick, tart lemon curd filling.
ingredients: 1 cup all-purpose flour, for the filling
steps: Heat the oven to 350F. Cream the butter and 1/2 cup sugar, then mix in the 2 cups flour and salt until it just comes together.
Press the dough into a 9x13 pan, building up a 1/2-inch edge all around - that lip is what keeps the filling from leaking underneath. Chill 20 minutes.
Bake the crust 15-20 minutes until lightly golden, then cool slightly. Baking it first stops the crust going soggy.
Whisk the eggs, 3 cups sugar, lemon zest, lemon juice and 1 cup flour until smooth, but do not beat in air.
Pour the filling onto the warm crust and bake 30-35 minutes until set and no longer wobbling in the center.
Cool completely, then chill 2 hours before cutting. Dust with powdered sugar just before serving - do it early and the sugar dissolves.

title: Tomato Soup with Grilled Cheese Croutons
description: Roasted tomato soup topped with cubes of grilled cheese sandwich.
steps: Toss the tomatoes with half the oil, the salt, pepper and sugar and roast cut-side up at 400F for 40 minutes until collapsed and caramelized at the edges.
Meanwhile cook the onions in the rest of the oil over medium heat 12 minutes until soft and sweet, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the roasted tomatoes with all their pan juices and the broth and simmer 15 minutes.
Blend with the basil until smooth, then return to the pot and stir in the cream over low heat. Do not let it boil after the cream goes in.
Make the grilled cheese: butter the bread, fill with Gruyere and griddle over medium-low until deep golden on both sides and fully melted.
Cut the sandwiches into 1-inch cubes and float them on the soup at the table, so they stay crisp.

title: Linguine with Shrimp Scampi
description: Shrimp in garlic lemon butter over linguine, with plenty of parsley.
steps: Boil the linguine in well-salted water to al dente and reserve a cup of the cooking water.
Melt 4 tbsp butter with the olive oil in a large skillet and cook the garlic over medium-low 1 minute. Do not let it brown or the whole dish turns bitter.
Pat the shrimp dry, season, and add them in a single layer. Cook 2-3 minutes, turning once, until just pink and curled into a loose C. A tight O means overcooked.
Take the pan off the heat and add the parsley, lemon zest, lemon juice, pepper flakes and remaining butter, swirling until it emulsifies.
Add the drained pasta and a splash of the cooking water and toss hard for a minute so the sauce clings.
Finish with the lemon slices and more parsley, and serve immediately.

title: Penne alla Vecchia Bettola
description: Vodka tomato sauce baked in the oven before tossing with penne.
ingredients: 2 cans (28 oz each) whole peeled tomatoes, drained
steps: Cook the onion in the olive oil in an oven-safe pot over medium heat 5 minutes, then add the garlic, oregano and pepper flakes for 1 minute.
Add the vodka and simmer until the volume is reduced by half, about 6 minutes. Reducing it properly cooks off the harshness and leaves the sharpness that makes this sauce work.
Crush the drained tomatoes by hand into the pot, season, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and bake at 375F for 1 1/2 hours. The long oven time is the whole trick: the sauce concentrates and sweetens in a way stovetop simmering does not match.
Puree the sauce with an immersion blender, then stir in the cream and heat through gently.
Toss with the cooked penne and a splash of pasta water, then finish with the basil and Parmesan.

title: Roasted Shrimp Cocktail
description: Shrimp roasted rather than boiled, with a horseradish chili sauce.
ingredients: 2 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
steps: Heat the oven to 400F. Toss the shrimp with the olive oil, salt and pepper and spread them in a single layer on a sheet pan.
Roast 8-10 minutes, just until pink and firm. Roasting concentrates the flavor instead of leaching it into water the way boiling does.
Cool the shrimp to room temperature, then refrigerate 30 minutes.
Stir the chili sauce, horseradish, lemon juice, Worcestershire and hot sauce together for the cocktail sauce.
Taste the sauce - it should be aggressively sharp, since it is cutting cold shrimp. Add more horseradish if it is timid.
Serve the chilled shrimp with the sauce and lemon wedges.

title: Parmesan Chicken
description: Thin breaded cutlets fried crisp and topped with dressed salad greens.
ingredients: 1/4 cup olive oil, for the dressing
steps: Pound the cutlets to an even 1/4 inch between sheets of plastic. Even thickness means they cook through before the crust burns.
Set up three dishes: flour seasoned with salt and pepper, the eggs beaten with the water, and the breadcrumbs mixed with the grated Parmesan.
Coat each cutlet in flour, then egg, then the crumb mixture, pressing it on firmly.
Heat the olive oil and 2 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-low. Lower heat than you expect - the Parmesan in the crust browns fast and will scorch over high heat.
Fry 2-3 minutes per side until deep golden, adding the remaining butter between batches. Drain on a rack.
Toss the greens with the olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper and pile the salad directly on top of each hot cutlet. Finish with shaved Parmesan.

title: Beatty's Chocolate Cake
description: A deep chocolate layer cake made with buttermilk and hot coffee.
ingredients: 1 tsp vanilla extract, for the frosting
steps: Heat the oven to 350F and line two 8-inch round pans. Sift the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda, baking powder and salt together.
Beat in the buttermilk, oil, eggs and vanilla until smooth.
With the mixer on low, pour in the hot coffee. The batter will be very thin - that is correct, and the coffee is what makes the chocolate taste like chocolate rather than sweet brown cake.
Divide between the pans and bake 35-40 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool 30 minutes in the pans, then turn out onto racks and cool completely.
Make the frosting: melt the chocolate and cool it, then beat the butter until light, add the egg yolk and vanilla, then the powdered sugar, then the melted chocolate and instant coffee.
Frost the top of the first layer, stack the second on, and frost the top. Never frost a warm cake - it slides straight off.

title: Cheddar Corn Chowder
description: Bacon, potato and corn chowder finished with sharp cheddar.
steps: Cook the bacon in the olive oil until crisp, then lift it out and reserve, leaving the fat.
Add the onions and cook 10 minutes until translucent, then stir in the turmeric, salt and pepper. The turmeric is mostly for the golden color.
Sprinkle over the flour and cook 2 minutes, stirring, then add the broth gradually so it stays smooth.
Add the potatoes and simmer 15 minutes until tender.
Add the corn and the half-and-half and heat through 5 minutes. Do not boil it after the dairy goes in.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the cheddar until melted. Serve topped with the crisp bacon and chives.

title: Herb-Roasted Turkey Breast
description: Bone-in turkey breast under a mustard, herb and wine paste.
steps: Heat the oven to 325F. Pat the turkey breast completely dry and set it skin-side up on a rack in a roasting pan.
Mash the mustard, all three herbs, the garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper into a thick paste.

Loosen the skin with your fingers and push some of the paste directly onto the meat, then spread the rest over the skin. Seasoning under the skin is what gets flavor into the meat rather than just on it.
Pour the wine into the bottom of the pan to keep the drippings from scorching.
Roast about 1 3/4 hours, until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 160F. Tent the skin with foil if it browns before the center is done.
Cover loosely and rest 15 minutes - the breast will coast to a safe 165F - then slice across the grain and spoon the pan juices over.

title: Easy Cranberry and Apple Cake
description: Tart fruit under a buttery batter that bakes into a crackly top.
ingredients: 2 Granny Smith apples, peeled and diced
steps: Heat the oven to 325F and butter a 10-inch pie dish.
Toss the cranberries, apples, orange zest, orange juice, brown sugar and cinnamon together and tip them into the dish in an even layer.
Beat the eggs and sugar on medium-high for a full 5 minutes until pale, thick and tripled in volume. This long whipping is the only leavening in the cake, so do not cut it short.
On low speed, add the melted butter, vanilla and almond extract, then the flour and salt, mixing only until combined.
Pour the batter over the fruit and spread it to cover completely, right to the edges.
Bake 55-60 minutes until the top is golden and a toothpick comes out clean. Serve warm with ice cream.

title: Garlic Roasted Potatoes
description: Halved small potatoes roasted crisp with whole garlic cloves.
ingredients: 3 lb small red or Yukon gold potatoes, halved
steps: Heat the oven to 400F. Toss the halved potatoes with the olive oil, salt and pepper.
Spread them cut-side down in a single layer on a sheet pan. Cut-side contact with hot metal is what gives you a flat golden crust on every piece.
Roast 45 minutes without disturbing them, until the undersides are deep brown and crisp.
Scatter the garlic over, toss, and roast 10 minutes more. Adding the garlic at the end keeps it from burning over the full roast.
Season again straight out of the oven while they are still hot.
Toss with the parsley and serve immediately.

title: Balsamic Roasted Brussels Sprouts
description: Sprouts roasted with pancetta until charred, finished with balsamic.
ingredients: 2 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
steps: Heat the oven to 425F. Toss the sprouts and pancetta with the olive oil, salt and pepper.
Spread them on a sheet pan with as many sprouts cut-side down as you can manage - those flat faces are where the caramelization happens.
Roast 30-35 minutes, shaking the pan once, until deeply browned and crisp at the edges. Let them get darker than feels comfortable; pale sprouts taste of nothing but cabbage.
Whisk the balsamic and honey together.
Toss the hot sprouts with the glaze right out of the oven.
Finish with Parmesan and serve immediately.

title: French Apple Tart
description: Thin apple slices on buttery pastry, glazed with apricot jam.
ingredients: 4 Granny Smith apples, peeled and cored
6 tbsp cold butter, diced, for the topping
steps: Pulse the flour, salt and 1 tbsp sugar, then cut in the cold butter until the largest pieces are pea-sized. Add the ice water and pulse until it just holds together when squeezed. Visible butter is what makes the pastry flaky.
Flatten into a disk, wrap and chill 1 hour. Then roll to a 13-inch square, set it on a parchment-lined sheet pan and chill again while you cut the apples.
Slice the apples as thinly and evenly as you can - 1/4 inch at most. Even slices cook at the same rate and lie flat.
Arrange them in tightly overlapping rows across the pastry, leaving a 1-inch border, then fold the border up over the edge.
Scatter the 1/2 cup sugar evenly over the apples and dot with the cold butter.

Bake at 400F for 45-55 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the apple edges are browned. Warm the jam with the calvados, strain it, and brush the hot tart all over to glaze. Cool before slicing.

title: Croque Monsieur
description: Ham and Gruyere sandwich under bechamel, broiled until bubbling.
steps: Toast the bread lightly on both sides and butter one side of each slice. Toasting first is what stops the sandwich collapsing under the sauce.
Melt the 4 tbsp butter, whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then add the warm milk gradually and simmer 3-4 minutes until thick. Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Off the heat, stir half the Gruyere and all the Parmesan into the sauce.
Spread Dijon on 4 slices, layer on the ham and some Gruyere, then cap with the remaining bread, buttered side up.
Set the sandwiches on a sheet pan, spoon the cheese sauce generously over the tops and scatter the rest of the Gruyere.
Bake at 400F for 5 minutes, then broil 3-5 minutes until the top is browned and bubbling. Watch it constantly under the broiler.

title: Rack of Lamb with Herbs
description: Racks marinated in rosemary, garlic and mustard, then roasted hot.
ingredients: 2 racks of lamb (8 bones each), trimmed
steps: Whisk the mustard, rosemary, garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper and rub it all over the lamb. Marinate 30 minutes at room temperature, or refrigerate overnight.
Heat the oven to 450F. Mix the panko, parsley and melted butter.
Set the racks fat-side up in a roasting pan and press the crumb mixture firmly onto the fat side.
Roast 20-25 minutes for medium-rare, to 128F internal. Use a thermometer - racks vary a lot in thickness and the window is narrow.
If the crust browns before the lamb is ready, tent it loosely with foil.
Rest 10 minutes, then carve between the bones into chops.

title: Summer Garden Pasta
description: Cherry tomatoes marinated for hours in oil and basil, tossed with hot pasta.
steps: Combine the halved tomatoes, olive oil, sliced garlic, basil, pepper flakes, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Cover and leave at room temperature for at least 4 hours, and up to 12. There is no cooking here at all - time is what breaks the tomatoes down into a sauce and takes the raw edge off the garlic.
Just before serving, boil the angel hair in well-salted water. It takes only 2-3 minutes, so have everything ready.
Drain the pasta and add it to the bowl of tomatoes while it is piping hot, tossing immediately. The heat of the pasta is what finishes the sauce.
Add half the Parmesan and toss again, loosening with a splash of pasta water if needed.
Serve at once with the rest of the Parmesan. Do not refrigerate the tomatoes at any point - cold kills their flavor.

title: Potato Fennel Gratin
description: Thin potatoes layered with sauteed fennel and Gruyere cream.
ingredients: 3 lb Yukon gold potatoes, sliced 1/8 inch thick
steps: Cook the fennel and onion in the olive oil and butter over medium-low heat for 15 minutes until completely soft and lightly golden. Raw fennel never softens properly in the oven, so this step is not optional.
Slice the potatoes thinly and evenly - a mandoline helps. Even thickness is what lets the gratin cook through uniformly.
Toss the potatoes with the cooked fennel mixture, the cream, 1 cup of the Gruyere, the salt, pepper and nutmeg in a large bowl.
Pour into a buttered 10x15 baking dish and press the top down flat so everything is submerged in cream.
Scatter the remaining Gruyere over and bake at 350F for 1 1/2 hours, until the top is browned and a knife slides through with no resistance.
Rest 20 minutes before serving so it sets enough to cut.

title: Plum Tarte Tatin
description: Plums caramelized in a skillet under pastry, then flipped out.
ingredients: 2 lb firm ripe plums, halved and pitted
steps: Melt the butter in a 10-inch oven-safe skillet, add the sugar and cook over medium heat 6-8 minutes, swirling rather than stirring, until it turns amber. Stirring caramel makes it crystallize.
Take it off the heat and arrange the plum halves cut-side up, packed tightly in concentric circles. They shrink considerably, so crowd them.
Return to medium heat for 10 minutes until the plums soften and release juice into the caramel. Add the vanilla and cinnamon.
Roll the puff pastry slightly larger than the pan, lay it over the fruit and tuck the edges down inside the pan rim.
Cut a few steam vents and bake at 400F for 30-35 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and puffed.

Rest exactly 10 minutes - long enough to stop the caramel running, short enough that it has not glued itself to the pan - then invert onto a platter in one confident motion. Serve warm with sweetened creme fraiche.
